title: Maths reference: Year 7 Algebra
summary: The words and methods from Year 7 Algebra, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards, one file per course (snippets/maths-<course>.json, split from the strand courses' files on 1 Nov 2026). code is TeX (shown typeset); hint may use $...$; unit is the course unit that introduces the card (its cheat sheet lists it); board is a maths-board setup drawn as the card's picture by tools/render-pictures.mjs; shows captions the picture.

items.label: formula
items.hint: A rule that gives one quantity from others, written with letters. This one gives the perimeter of a rectangle.
items.board:
widget: formula
formula: P = 2l + 2w
slider l: 1, 10, 5
slider w: 1, 6, 3
shape: rectangle
units: cm

items.label: variable
items.hint: A letter for a quantity that can change. Each rectangle has its own $l$, $w$ and $P$.

items.label: constant
items.hint: A number that stays the same, such as a 20 dollar call-out fee. $\pi$ is a constant too.

items.label: unknown
items.hint: In an equation, a letter can stand for one particular number: here only $x = 4$ works.

items.label: more than, less than
items.hint: "5 more than n" is $n + 5$. "5 less than n" is $n - 5$: you start from $n$ and take 5 away, so $n$ comes first.

items.label: brackets
items.hint: Brackets keep a part together so it is worked out first. "Add 3, then double the result" is $2(n + 3)$; "double, then add 3" is $2n + 3$.

items.label: expression
items.hint: A calculation with a letter in it. It has a value once you know the letter, but it does not say that anything is equal.

items.label: equation
items.hint: Two expressions with = between them: a statement that they are equal, like a balanced scale.
items.board:
widget: balance
left: 2x + 3
right: 11
min: 0
max: 10
start: 4

items.label: solution
items.hint: The value of the letter that makes the equation true.

items.label: 2x means 2 times x
items.hint: With $x = 4$, $2x$ is 8, not 24.

items.label: inverse operations
items.hint: Each step has an opposite that undoes it: adding and subtracting, multiplying and dividing.

items.label: write an expression for a situation
items.hint: Say what the letter stands for (a number that changes), multiply it by the amount for each one, then add anything paid once.

items.label: substitute
items.hint: Replace each letter with its value, write in the × signs, then work it out: brackets, then × and ÷, then + and −.

items.label: find an unknown in a formula
items.hint: Substitute what you know, then solve the equation that is left by undoing. Check by substituting back.

items.label: check by substitution
items.hint: Put the value in place of the letter and work out both sides. If they match, it is a solution. Check every answer in the first equation.

items.label: backtracking
items.hint: Undo the steps done to $x$ with their opposites, last step first.
items.shows: Multiply by 3, then add 7. Undo + 7 first.

items.label: balance method
items.hint: Do the same to both sides (take away, or share into equal groups) until $x$ is on its own.
items.board:
widget: balance
left: 3x + 5
right: 20
min: 0
max: 10
start: 5
items.shows: Take 5 from both sides, then share both into 3 groups.

items.label: x on both sides
items.hint: Take the same number of $x$ from both sides first, so the bags are on one side only.

items.label: growing pattern
items.hint: What each new figure adds goes in front of $n$; what is there at the start goes on its own. Figure 4 has $3 \times 4 + 1 = 13$ sticks.
items.board:
widget: pattern
shape: squares
n: 1, 8, 4
count: on
items.shows: Figure 4: each square adds 3 sticks, plus 1 at the start

items.label: rule
items.hint: A rule turns each input $x$ into an output $y$. Put the input in for $x$: $x = 3$ gives $y = 2 \times 3 + 1 = 7$.

items.label: table of values
items.hint: Choose inputs, work out each output from the rule ($y = 2x + 1$ here), and write them in pairs.

items.label: ordered pair
items.hint: Input first, then output. To plot it: across 2 on the $x$-axis, then up 5.
items.board:
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -1, 8
point A: 2, 5

items.label: reading a graph
items.hint: Find the value you know on its axis, go to the line, then read across to the other axis. Sections of a graph increase, decrease or stay constant.

items.label: vary one variable
items.code: V = l \times w \times h \quad (\text{change } h \text{ only})
items.hint: To see what one letter does, change only that letter and keep the others the same. Record the results in a table.
